key_insight: This paper shows how to trace which instruction words influence specific parts of generated speech in style-captioned text-to-speech. By adapting cross-attention attribution to speech diffusion models, it makes expressive TTS more interpretable and easier to debug.
problem_solved: Style-captioned TTS can follow natural-language style prompts, but it is unclear how individual words in the caption affect acoustic output. This lack of transparency makes it hard to diagnose failures, understand controllability, or improve generation quality.
method: Adapts DAAM-style cross-attention attribution from image generation to speech diffusion models for the first time.
Computes per-token heatmaps across 25 layers to estimate how each instruction word contributes to the generated speech.
Applies the attribution method to CapSpeech-TTS to analyze word-level control and reveal failure modes in expressive TTS.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a practical interpretability tool for speech generation models. It can help debug prompt-following errors, improve prompt design, and build more reliable controllable TTS systems.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing caption text flowing into a TTS diffusion model with attention maps over speech frames.
Per-token heatmaps highlighting which words affect pitch, emotion, or speaking style.
Layer-wise attribution chart showing attention strength across 25 layers.
Before/after examples of captions and the resulting speech style to illustrate controllability.
paper_title: How Do Instructions Shape Speech? Cross-Attention Attribution for Style-Captioned Text-to-Speech
paper_authors: Nityanand Mathur, Hamees Sayed, Wasim Madha, Apoorv Singh, Sameer Khurana
